title: MCP + RAG Orchestration
summary: An orchestrated AI assistant over company knowledge and tools: a RAG pipeline (ingest, chunk, embed, hybrid retrieve, rerank) built with LangChain, a LangGraph state machine that routes between retrieval, MCP tools and human review, and LangSmith for tracing and evaluation.

blocks.text: Framing: an internal assistant for a bank's operations team that answers questions from policies, runbooks and tickets with citations, and can take actions (look up a trade, open a Jira ticket, query a database) through MCP servers.

head: Type
Requirement
rows: Ask questions; get grounded answers with citations to source documents
Call tools: Jira, Confluence, SQL read replicas, internal APIs — via MCP
Multi-turn conversations; human approval before write actions
Answers respect document permissions (user sees only what they may read)
Every run traceable and evaluated; regression tests on prompt/model changes

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: The corpus fits comfortably in one vector cluster; the hard parts are retrieval quality, permission filtering, and orchestrating tools safely.

items: Open protocol (introduced by Anthropic, now widely adopted) that standardizes how AI applications connect to tools and data — 'USB-C for AI integrations'.
**Roles:** a *host* (the AI app) runs one *client* per connection to an MCP *server*; servers expose capabilities.
**Server primitives:** *tools* (functions the model can call, with JSON-schema inputs), *resources* (readable data identified by URIs), *prompts* (reusable templates).
**Client features** servers may request: *sampling* (ask the host's model for a completion), *roots* (filesystem boundaries), *elicitation* (ask the user for input).
**Wire format:** JSON-RPC 2.0 with capability negotiation in `initialize`; `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `resources/read`, notifications for list changes.
**Transports:** stdio for local servers; Streamable HTTP (with optional SSE streaming) for remote servers; OAuth 2.1-based authorization for remote servers.
M apps × N integrations becomes M + N, like LSP did for editors.

blocks.title: Trap
blocks.text: An MCP server's tool descriptions and outputs are untrusted input to the model. Pin and review servers, scope their credentials, and require approval for write tools.

items.title: Ingest
items.text: Connectors (Confluence, SharePoint, Jira) via loaders or CDC; store raw + metadata (ACLs, owner, updated_at).

items.title: Chunk
items.text: Structure-aware splitting (headings, tables) ~300–800 tokens with overlap; keep parent-document links.

items.title: Embed
items.text: Batch embeddings; store vector + text + metadata; version the embedding model.

items.title: Retrieve
items.text: Hybrid: BM25 + vector kNN with metadata/ACL filters; reciprocal rank fusion.

items.title: Rerank
items.text: Cross-encoder reranker on top ~50 → top 5–8 chunks.

items.title: Generate
items.text: Prompt with numbered sources; require citations; refuse when context is insufficient.

head: Technique
Fixes
rows: Short queries that don't match document wording
Small chunks match, big context answers
Chunks that lose meaning out of context

blocks.caption: LangGraph orchestrates; retrieval and MCP tools are nodes; LangSmith sees everything

sections.title: Deep dive: the LangGraph state machine

blocks.text:
class State(TypedDict):
    messages: Annotated[list, add_messages]
    docs: list
    route: str

g = StateGraph(State)
g.add_node('classify', classify_intent)      # question | action | chit-chat
g.add_node('retrieve', hybrid_retrieve)      # ACL-filtered hybrid search + rerank
g.add_node('grade', grade_documents)         # drop irrelevant chunks; maybe rewrite query
g.add_node('generate', answer_with_citations)
g.add_node('agent', tool_agent)              # LLM with MCP tools bound
g.add_node('approve', human_approval)        # interrupt() before write tools
g.add_edge(START, 'classify')
g.add_conditional_edges('classify', lambda s: s['route'], {'question': 'retrieve', 'action': 'agent'})
g.add_edge('retrieve', 'grade')
g.add_conditional_edges('grade', enough_context, {True: 'generate', False: 'retrieve'})   # corrective RAG loop (max 2)
g.add_conditional_edges('agent', needs_approval, {True: 'approve', False: END})
g.add_edge('approve', 'agent')
g.add_edge('generate', END)
app = g.compile(checkpointer=PostgresSaver(conn))   # thread_id = conversation

items: Checkpointer persists state per `thread_id`: conversations resume, crashes recover, approvals can wait hours.
`interrupt()` pauses before a write tool; the UI shows the proposed action; `Command(resume=...)` continues.
Bound loops (max retrieval retries, max tool steps) in state.
Stream tokens and intermediate steps to the UI.
Document ACLs copied into chunk metadata at ingest; retrieval always filters by the user's groups (pre-filter, not post-filter, so top-k isn't emptied).
MCP servers run with per-user OAuth tokens or narrowly scoped service credentials; SQL tools hit read replicas with row-level security and query timeouts.
Allowlist MCP servers and tools per assistant; pin versions; review tool descriptions for injected instructions.
Write tools require approval; all calls audited with user, tool, arguments, result.
PII redaction before logging to LangSmith where required; data residency for traces.

items.q: Why MCP instead of plain function calling?
items.a: Function calling is how a model asks for a tool; MCP standardizes how tools are discovered, described, authorized and transported, so any MCP-capable host can reuse the same Jira or database server.

items.q: How do you choose chunk size?
items.a: Empirically with retrieval evals: smaller chunks raise precision, larger ones keep context; parent-document retrieval gets both.
When answers require connecting many entities (e.g. 'which counterparties are affected by this settlement change?'); build an entity graph and retrieve subgraphs.

items.q: LangGraph vs a plain LangChain agent?
items.a: LangGraph gives explicit control flow, persistence, interrupts and bounded loops — needed for production workflows with approvals.

items: MCP: host/client/server; tools, resources, prompts; JSON-RPC; stdio or Streamable HTTP.
RAG: ingest → chunk → embed → hybrid retrieve → rerank → cite.
LangChain = components; LangGraph = stateful graph + checkpoints + interrupts; LangSmith = traces + evals.
Filter by ACL at retrieval time.
Approvals before write tools; treat retrieved text and tool output as untrusted.
Eval retrieval and groundedness in CI.
